text: dsh-sensevoice-npu 是面向 DSH 桌面语音输入的本地语音转文字插件。它向语音服务注册 SenseVoiceSmall provider，并由 Python worker 通过 OpenVINO 在 Intel NPU 上执行识别，同时可用 CPU 运行 VAD。用户可用语音输入转写中文、英文、粤语、日语或韩语，并处理分段和较长录音。插件沿用 DSH 的语音输入界面与准备流程；使用前需要准备模型文件、Python 环境和 Intel NPU 驱动，不需要 API 密钥，也不会由插件下载模型。

dsh-sensevoice-npu adds local SenseVoiceSmall transcription to DSH voice input. A Python worker uses OpenVINO on an Intel NPU, with optional CPU VAD. It supports Chinese, English, Cantonese, Japanese and Korean. Provide model files, Python and an NPU driver; no API key or model download is needed.
想让 DSH 的语音输入在本机 Intel NPU 上做语音转文字。
能不能用 SenseVoice 把中文或英文录音转成文字？
I want DSH voice input to transcribe speech locally with an Intel NPU.
dsh-sensevoice-npu 的功能「本地语音转文字」：DSH 语音服务调用 SenseVoiceSmall，将录音交给本机 Python worker 识别并返回文本；支持中文、英文、粤语、日语和韩语。
dsh-sensevoice-npu 的功能「语音准备与分段识别」：语音服务准备时检查解释器和模型文件，启动 worker 并可预热指定帧长；识别时支持 VAD 分段，较长输入按帧桶切块，返回拼接后的文本。

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · dsh-sensevoice-npu：Local speech-to-text for DSH that runs **SenseVoiceSmall on the Intel NPU**
through OpenVINO, plugged into the official voice-input stack.

It registers one more provider into the stock
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-speech-to-text` service, so the voice-input
button, the settings card, the preparation UI and the speech API keep working
unchanged — only the recognizer behind them changes.

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Why a separate plugin：The bundled provider (`dsh-experimental-speech-to-text-sensevoice`) is CPU-only
by construction:

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Why a separate plugin：This plugin sidesteps all four: it bakes `x_length` into a constant for one
frame bucket (which the NPU compiler accepts), compiles that graph for the NPU,
and serves it through a small Python worker.

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Layout：| Path | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/index.js` | cordis plugin: registers the provider, spawns the worker, runs preparation |
| `lib/worker.py` | authenticated loopback HTTP worker (one WAV per request) |
| `lib/sensevoice_npu.py` | frontend (fbank + LFR + CMVN), Silero VAD, NPU session, CTC decode |
| `runtime/bootstrap.ps1` | creates the virtual environment the worker needs |

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Layout：The frontend mirrors sherpa-onnx exactly: `kaldi_native_fbank` with the same
options, `ApplyLfr` (7/6), and `(x + neg_mean) * inv_stddev` with the CMVN
vectors read from the ONNX metadata — so transcripts match the CPU provider.

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Prerequisite: model files：The worker reads three files (this plugin does **not** download models — it registers with an empty `downloadSources`):

| Path relative to `dataRoot` | Size |
| --- | --- |
| `models/sensevoice-onnx/model.int8.onnx` | ~228 MB |
| `models/sensevoice-onnx/tokens.txt` | ~0.3 MB |
| `models/silero/silero_vad.onnx` | ~1.7 MB |

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Prerequisite: model files：The official `dsh-experimental-speech-to-text-sensevoice` provider downloads them into the same `dataRoot` (`<DSH home>/speech-to-text/sensevoice`), so let that provider prepare once, or place the files at those paths yourself.

1. Build the Python environment (needs a 64-bit Python 3.11–3.13 and the Intel
   NPU driver):

```powershell
   pwsh -File runtime/bootstrap.ps1
   ```

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Prerequisite: model files：2. Install the package into the profile that owns the voice-input bundle (the
   DSH desktop app uses the `desktop` profile):

```powershell
   dsh plugin --profile desktop add "file:C:/path/to/dsh-sensevoice-npu"
   ```

pnpm copies the package, so while iterating on it replace the copy with a
   junction to your working tree:

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Prerequisite: model files：```powershell
   $d = "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-sensevoice-npu"
   Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $d
   New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path $d -Target C:\path\to\dsh-sensevoice-npu
   ```

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Prerequisite: model files：3. The bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml` already selects the provider and registers
   the plugin, and it contains **no machine-specific path**: `pythonPath` and
   `dataRoot` default to the `bootstrap.ps1` venv and DSH's speech root. Append an
   override to `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml` (back it up first) only
   when you moved either one:

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Prerequisite: model files：```yaml
   - id: speech-to-text-npu
     name: 'dsh-sensevoice-npu'
     config:
       pythonPath: <custom venv>\Scripts\python.exe   # only with -VenvDir

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Prerequisite: model files：4. Restart DSH. The voice-input card then lists
   *SenseVoiceSmall · Intel NPU (NPU)* and uses it by default; the first
   preparation compiles the NPU graph once (~2.5 min), after which starts take
   ~0.2 s. If the card still shows the CPU provider, pick the NPU one in the
   voice-input settings (an explicit choice persists over the patch default).

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pythonPath` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-sensevoice-npu\venv\Scripts\python.exe` | worker interpreter (`runtime/bootstrap.ps1` target) |
| `dataRoot` | `<DSH home>/speech-to-text/sensevoice` | DSH speech root; models are read from `<dataRoot>/models` |
| `precision` | `int8` | `int8` (`model.int8.onnx`) or `fp32` (`model.onnx`) |
| `device` | `NPU` | OpenVINO device for the recogniser (`NPU`, `GPU`, `CPU`) |
| `vadDevice` | `CPU` | Silero VAD device — tiny model, dynamic shapes, NPU rejects it |
| `useVad` | `true` | trim silence and split long speech into segments |
| `buckets` | `[64, 96, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 768, 1024]` (plugin config sets `[256]`) | LFR-frame buckets the engine may compile |
| `prewarmBuckets` | `[256]` | buckets compiled before the worker reports ready |
| `idleTimeoutMs` | `600000` | release the worker after idling; compiled blobs stay cached |

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Configuration：Each bucket costs roughly 800 MB on disk (baked IR + OpenVINO NPU cache) and one
~2.5 minute compile the first time. One bucket is enough for dictation: 256
frames ≈ 15 s of audio, and the NPU handles the padding cheaply.

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Measured behaviour (Core Ultra X7 358H, Arc B390, NPU driver 32.0.100.5540)：| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Warm start (compiled blob cached) | 0.21 s |
| 4.5 s Chinese clip → 256-frame bucket | `今天天气不错，我们去公园散步吧`, 0.66 s inference |
| 5.2 s clip | `明天上午10点开会，记得带上项目进度报告`, 0.48 s |
| 14.5 s clip | full sentence correct, 0.65 s |
| First compile per bucket | 100–145 s, cached afterwards |

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Measured behaviour (Core Ultra X7 358H, Arc B390, NPU driver 32.0.100.5540)：CPU is used only for the frontend (fbank + VAD, a few ms) and JSON plumbing; the
encoder/decoder graph runs on the NPU. Note that the NPU is *not* faster than
sherpa-onnx on CPU for clips this short (~0.5 s vs ~0.2 s) — the win is moving
the heavy work off the CPU/GPU entirely.

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Development：```sh
node --test        # 6 tests, no dependencies
```

They cover the registration contract (provider id, device label, diagnostic file),
the portable `pythonPath`/`dataRoot` defaults, and the two config guards that
would otherwise fail much later: an empty bucket list and a relative path.

dsh-sensevoice-npu README · Troubleshooting：* Confirm the profile really loaded the plugin and see the last phase/device:

```powershell
  Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\speech-to-text\sensevoice\npu\provider-status.json"
  ```

* `NPU device not visible` → update the Intel NPU driver (32.0.100.5540 tested).
* `NPU compile failed` → delete `<dataRoot>/npu` and retry; check free disk
  (~1 GB per bucket).
* Transcription slow on first use of a new bucket → it is compiling; later runs
  reuse the cache.
